bibl.title: Circ-ZNF609 Is a Circular RNA that Can Be Translated and Functions in Myogenesis

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: circular RNAs in myogenesis, and one of them - circ-ZNF609 - which turns out to be translated into protein
span.quote: Here we performed expression profiling of circRNAs during in vitro differentiation of murine and human myoblasts, and we identified conserved species regulated in myogenesis and altered in Duchenne muscular dystrophy.

span.label: which circRNAs are regulated during muscle differentiation, and what any of them actually does
span.quote: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) constitute a family of transcripts with unique structures and still largely unknown functions. Their biogenesis, which proceeds via a back-splicing reaction, is fairly well characterized, whereas their role in the modulation of physiologically relevant processes is still unclear.

span.label: an expression screen across murine and human myoblasts, a functional screen narrowing to 31 candidates, and the demonstration that one circRNA is cap-independently translated
span.quote: Circ-ZNF609 is associated with heavy polysomes, and it is translated into a protein in a splicing-dependent and cap-independent manner, providing an example of a protein-coding circRNA in eukaryotes.

span.label: existence
span.quote: Circ-ZNF609 is associated with heavy polysomes, and it is translated into a protein in a splicing-dependent and cap-independent manner, providing an example of a protein-coding circRNA in eukaryotes.

span.label: covalently closed RNA circles, produced by back-splicing, which lack a cap and a poly-A tail and are nonetheless found on heavy polysomes
span.quote: Another relevant aspect about circRNAs, lacking the cap structure and the polyA tail, relates to the machinery and factors required for the assembly into translationally competent complexes.

span.label: circRNA expression profiling during myoblast differentiation, RNAi functional screening filtered on four criteria, and polysome association plus reporter assays for translation
span.term: circRNA expression profiling during myoblast differentiation, RNAi functional screening filtered on four criteria, and polysome association plus reporter assays for translation
span.quote: Specific criteria were applied in order to restrict the number of candidates for further characterization: (1) conservation, (2) expression level, (3) modulation during differentiation, and (4) circular/linear ratio (see the STAR Methods ). This filtering yielded 31 circRNAs

span.label: circ-ZNF609 carries an open reading frame that starts at the linear transcript's start codon and ends at a STOP codon CREATED BY CIRCULARISATION - the circle makes the frame that the linear molecule does not have
span.quote: Circ-ZNF609 is associated with heavy polysomes, and it is translated into a protein in a splicing-dependent and cap-independent manner, providing an example of a protein-coding circRNA in eukaryotes.

span.label: translation happens without a cap or a poly-A tail, so the initiation machinery must be the IRES route - first described in VIRAL RNAs and later found in cellular ones
span.quote: Cap-independent translation, driven by the so-called IRES, was initially described in viral RNAs ( Pelletier and Sonenberg, 1988 ) and subsequently identified also in cellular RNAs

span.label: THE CAUSAL BRIDGE BETWEEN THE PAPER'S TWO FINDINGS IS DECLARED MISSING: plasmids, expression vectors and naked RNA all produced a non-specific block of proliferation, so the authors `were UNABLE TO PERFORM RESCUE EXPERIMENTS AND UNIVOCALLY LINK the circ-ZNF609 phenotype to its protein-coding capacity`
span.quote: However, since the use of plasmids and other expression vectors as well as naked RNA produced a non-specific block of myoblast proliferation, we were unable to perform rescue experiments and univocally link the circ-ZNF609 phenotype to its protein-coding capacity.

span.label: and the alternative readings are left open rather than argued away - the protein `could act as a dominant-negative competitor OR as a modulator of alternative ZNF609 complex formation`
span.quote: it could act as a dominant-negative competitor or as a modulator of alternative ZNF609 complex formation.

span.label: the field's own headline mechanism does not generalise: genome-wide studies show that miRNA sponging CANNOT BE GENERALLY APPLIED, and other mechanisms have had to be proposed
span.quote: Nevertheless, genome-wide studies have demonstrated that miRNA sponging activity cannot be generally applied ( Memczak et al., 2013 , You et al., 2015 , Jeck and Sharpless, 2014 ), and other mechanisms have also been proposed, such as acting as platforms for protein interaction

span.label: and the first sentence of the abstract concedes the state of the field: circRNAs are `a family of transcripts with unique structures and STILL LARGELY UNKNOWN FUNCTIONS`, their role in physiologically relevant processes `still unclear`
span.quote: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) constitute a family of transcripts with unique structures and still largely unknown functions. Their biogenesis, which proceeds via a back-splicing reaction, is fairly well characterized, whereas their role in the modulation of physiologically relevant processes is still unclear.

span.label: the functional screen is filtered on four stated criteria before anything is characterised - conservation, expression level, modulation during differentiation, and the circular/linear ratio
span.note: eliminates: a candidate chosen after the fact from whatever the screen happened to show; the filter yielded 31 and it was declared before the phenotypes · outcome: held
span.quote: Specific criteria were applied in order to restrict the number of candidates for further characterization: (1) conservation, (2) expression level, (3) modulation during differentiation, and (4) circular/linear ratio (see the STAR Methods ). This filtering yielded 31 circRNAs

span.label: whether the proliferation phenotype is caused by the PROTEIN circ-ZNF609 encodes
span.note: eliminates: nothing - plasmids, expression vectors and naked RNA all produced a non-specific block, so the rescue experiment that would link them could not be done · outcome: failed
span.quote: However, since the use of plasmids and other expression vectors as well as naked RNA produced a non-specific block of myoblast proliferation, we were unable to perform rescue experiments and univocally link the circ-ZNF609 phenotype to its protein-coding capacity.

span.label: whether circRNA induction simply tracks the transcription of its host gene
span.note: eliminates: a circRNA change that is only a gene-expression change - and the exception is reported: circ-BNC2 predominates in differentiated cells while its gene makes mainly linear mRNA in growing ones · outcome: partial
span.quote: However, exceptions were detected, such as the BNC2 gene that produces mainly the linear mRNA in human and mouse myoblasts in growth conditions but predominantly the circRNA in differentiated cells.

span.label: circRNAs
span.quote: RNA molecules lacking 5′ and 3′ ends and shaped as covalently closed circular RNAs (circRNAs) were described decades ago in a variety of model systems, but they were considered rare events

span.label: circRNA, AS THE CATEGORY STOOD BEFORE 2012: `described decades ago in a variety of model systems, BUT THEY WERE CONSIDERED RARE EVENTS`. A class of molecule inside the error term
span.quote: RNA molecules lacking 5′ and 3′ ends and shaped as covalently closed circular RNAs (circRNAs) were described decades ago in a variety of model systems, but they were considered rare events

span.label: circRNA, AFTER salzman2012 - WHICH THIS PAPER CITES BY NAME FOR EXACTLY THAT: `commonly produced by thousands of genes`. The corpus holds both sides of this citation, and the pair is the category moving
span.quote: However, recent studies report that these molecules are commonly produced by thousands of genes

span.label: circRNA, AFTER THIS PAPER: protein-coding, at least sometimes. AND THE KEYWORD LIST OF THIS VERY ARTICLE STILL READS `non-coding RNA`. The class is filed under a property the paper disproves for one of its members
span.quote: Circ-ZNF609 is associated with heavy polysomes, and it is translated into a protein in a splicing-dependent and cap-independent manner, providing an example of a protein-coding circRNA in eukaryotes.

span.label: the exception that shows the rule is not one - circ-BNC2: its gene produces mainly the LINEAR mRNA in growing myoblasts and PREDOMINANTLY THE CIRCULAR form in differentiated cells. Which isoform is `the` transcript depends on the cell state
span.quote: However, exceptions were detected, such as the BNC2 gene that produces mainly the linear mRNA in human and mouse myoblasts in growth conditions but predominantly the circRNA in differentiated cells.

span.label: extends → Salzman et al. 2012, cited here for the finding that circRNAs are commonly produced by thousands of genes - the result that moved them out of the error term
span.quote: However, recent studies report that these molecules are commonly produced by thousands of genes

span.note: WHOSE RESULT THIS IS: studies have demonstrated - 2026-08-26 terminal-a. THE SUBJECT OF THIS RESULT IS AN INDEFINITE STUDY, NOT THIS PAPER. `Previous studies reported`, `studies in guinea pig showed`, `recent studies have reported` - somebody else's work under a common noun rather than a name, with a citation in the sentence and no first-person marker. The quote is verbatim and the claim is true; only the attribution is wrong. FOUND BY MEASURING MY OWN CUE'S RECALL: the first sweep required a NAMED author as the subject (`Sperling (1960) demonstrated`) and found 17. Reading eleven citation-bearing findings on `Plakke2016` by hand showed four the cue could not see - `A study examining recognition found`, `studies of typical human subjects have demonstrated`, `A follow up study found` - so the named cue's 17 was a floor and not a count. A CUE'S FALSE POSITIVES TELL YOU NOTHING ABOUT ITS FALSE NEGATIVES, and the only way to find these was to read a record's whole layer. Q-1118.
